Beyond the pulpit,
into an age when everyone reads the Bible for themselves
BIBLY 바이블 인사이트는, 평신도가 누구의 해석에도 휘둘리지 않고 성: BIBLY Bible Insight is an online academy devoted to the Bible and the end times, helping lay believers read the Bible for themselves without being swayed by anyone's interpretation.
우리는 <b class=\"text-neutral-900\">한국 교회를: We love the Korean church. Built on the tears and devotion of countless believers, this church — we long, more than anyone, for it to become the light of the world once again. Yet at some point we found ourselves watching the church, which ought to be a light, grow darker instead: factional fighting and division, a prosperity faith that only asks for blessings, a religious pluralism that calls everything right, and a church that has lost its essence being swept along into extremes and deception. — Watching the church lose what makes it the church, our hearts have ached for a long time.
그러나 우리가 정말로 외면할 수 없었던 것은, <b class=\"tex: But what we truly could not turn away from were the countless souls who, in spite of it all, cannot bring themselves to leave the sanctuary and quietly keep their place. People who thirst for the truth yet have never heard a satisfying answer anywhere, whose souls are quietly drying up. We could not pretend not to see that thirst.
멀리 미국 신학대학원에서 <b class=\"text-neutral-90: Studying far away at a theological graduate school in the United States, pouring ourselves into it to the bone, we were reminded of just one thing — that we must return to the Bible, to the essence of the church. Not dazzling fame or anyone's authority, but raising up believers who read and discern the Bible for themselves, unshaken by anyone's interpretation.
그래서 우리는 이 길을 시작했습니다. 무너진 강단을 비난하기 위해서가 아: That is why we set out on this road. Not to condemn pulpits that have fallen, but to awaken the Korean church of this generation once again. Not to make people lean on one person's pulpit, but to raise up, together, believers who stand before the Word for themselves. It is a small step, but together with you, who share the same heart, we can surely rise again. — Will you walk this road with us?
“성경을 스스로 읽는 눈을 길러,<br class=\"hidden sm::
“We grow eyes that read the Bible for themselves,
and raise up unshakable people of discernment.”
한 사람의 강단이 아니라,<br class=\"sm:hidden\"> 만: Not one person's pulpit,<br class="sm:hidden"> but a movement that opens ten thousand pairs of eyes
사람의 권위나 전통, 교권이 아니라 <b class=\"text-neut: Not human authority, tradition or church hierarchy — only the written Word is the final authority for faith and life.
성직자만의 특권이 아닙니다. <b class=\"text-neutral-: It is not the privilege of the clergy alone. Every believer comes directly to God and reads and delights in the Word for themselves.
믿음은 강요될 수 없습니다. 사람은 누구나 <b class=\"text-: Faith cannot be forced. Every person believes and responds before God for themselves, and no power may stand over that conscience.
물려받거나 형식이 된 신앙이 아니라, <b class=\"text-neu: We stand not on a faith that is inherited or has become a mere formality, but on a faith each person has come to understand and confess for themselves. Baptism, too, is received upon that confession.
유행과 두려움, 거짓 가르침에 휩쓸리지 않습니다. <b class=\"t: We are not swept along by trends, fear or false teaching. Testing all things by the Word, we stay awake and discern the times.

신학과 인문학, 그리고 교육학을 공부하며 깨달은 한 가지가 있습니다. 신: Studying theology, the humanities and education, I came to realize one thing: a crisis of faith always begins with ‘not being able to read the Bible for oneself.’
그래서 이 사역은 강단의 권위를 내세우기보다, <b class=\"tex: So rather than putting forward the authority of the pulpit, this ministry focuses on helping each and every lay believer open the Bible directly and grow the eyes to discern the times. I want to turn difficult theology into plain language, and the fear of the end times into the confidence of discernment.
무엇이든 편하게 물어보세요. 정답을 몰라도 괜찮습니다. <b class=: Feel free to ask anything. It's all right if you don't know the answer. I invite you to the road of reading the Bible together and finding the answers together.
<a href=\"find.html\" class=\"bg-gold te: Find the Right Course → Ask anything
수강생이 강사의 신학적 뿌리를 알고 <b class=\"text-neut: So that students can know their teacher's theological roots and learn with trust, we lay that foundation out openly. Lead teacher Oh Kwang-il studied in the Master of Bible Studies program at West Coast Baptist College in the United States and is the lead translator of the “King James Bible — Jeongbon Translation”, which is based on the Received Text (Textus Receptus). Every BIBLY course stands consistently on the theological tradition of the Independent Baptist churches.
독립 침례교는 19세기 후반, 남침례교(SBC)를 비롯한 기성 교단이 시: The Independent Baptist movement grew out of the Fundamentalist movement of the late nineteenth century, which sought to return to the absolute authority of the Bible and its fundamental truths at a time when established denominations, including the Southern Baptist Convention (SBC), were changing with the currents of the age. The churches and pastors who carried this movement forward founded schools such as Hyles-Anderson College, West Coast Baptist College, Pensacola Christian College and Bob Jones University, and among them, First Baptist Church of Hammond and Lancaster Baptist Church are counted today among the most influential churches in America. BIBLY is deeply rooted in this very tradition of proven, conservative faith.
성경은 하나님의 영감으로 기록된, 신앙과 삶의 <b class=\"tex: The Bible, written by the inspiration of God, is the final authority for faith and life.
성경을 임의의 비유로 흩뜨리지 않고 <b class=\"text-neut: We do not scatter the Bible into arbitrary allegories; we read and explain it just as the text says.
이스라엘과 교회를 구분하며, <b class=\"text-neutral-: We distinguish between Israel and the church, and we look forward to the pretribulation rapture and the literal thousand-year reign of Christ.
구원은 행위가 아니라 <b class=\"text-neutral-900/: Salvation is given not by works but by the grace of Christ, through faith.
광야에서 다시 만난<br class=\"sm:hidden\"> 부활의 주: The risen Lord<br class="sm:hidden"> I met again in the wilderness
세 살, 아직 아버지의 얼굴조차 또렷이 기억하지 못하던 나이에 저는 아버: I lost my father when I was three — too young even to remember his face clearly. In a place where only poverty and grief remained, my mother, now alone, raised me in tears, vowing, ‘If only You will keep this son safe, I will give him to You as Your servant.’ Death and poverty had arrived first, in the place of my very earliest memories.
그런 제게 시골의 작은 교회는 온 세상이었습니다. 그곳은 동네 아이들의: For a boy like me, the small country church was the whole world. It was the neighborhood children's playground, library and gym where we ran around together. When my heart felt cold, I would sit alone in the empty sanctuary, look up at the cross, and pour out to God in tears the sorrow of having no father, and our poverty. It was a community like a warm embrace, and every time it helped me feel the God who was always with me.
그 교회의 품에서 저는 자연스레 <b class=\"text-neutra: In the arms of that church, I naturally grew a dream of becoming a pastor who preaches the word of life from the pulpit. But as I grew into my teens, I began to see another face of the church. Long-held old ways and factions, envy and jealousy, whispering behind people's backs… Even a community that looked holy had deep shadows. Seeing all this, one honest question began to grow in my heart: ‘What kind of person is a pastor — a true minister — really?’
어른이 되어서도 그 질문은 저를 떠나지 않았습니다. 어머니의 서원이 늘: Even as an adult, that question never left me. My mother's vow always weighed on my heart like a debt, but I did not want to become a pastor just because I felt sorry about that debt. Still less did I want to enjoy the prestige of being called ‘Pastor, Pastor’ from the pulpit. What should a true minister look like in this age? — Unable to find that answer, I buried my dream of ministry deep in my heart for a while. I studied hard, worked faithfully, met my wise and beautiful wife, and lived day by day as the father of two daughters and an ordinary office worker.
그렇게 마음 한편에 오랜 물음을 품고 살아가던 어느 날, 저를 믿음으로: I was living like that, an old question tucked away in a corner of my heart, when one day the grandfather who had raised me in the faith passed away. At his funeral, as the Scripture was read, one verse struck my heart like a clap of thunder.
“나는 부활이요 생명이니, 나를 믿는 자는 죽어도 살겠고, 살아서 나를: “I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live: And whosoever liveth and believeth in me shall never die.”— John 11:25–26
어린 시절 아버지의 죽음 앞에서 묻기 시작한 그 질문의 답이, 바로 그: The answer to the question I had begun asking as a child, standing before my father's death, came to me right there — in the living Jesus. Only then did I know, with my whole being, that death is not the end, and that He who is the resurrection and the life is the answer to everything. And I made my decision — to give the rest of my life wholly to proclaiming Jesus, who is the resurrection and the life for all people.
저에게는 <b class=\"text-neutral-900\">십오 년: There was a church I had served for nearly fifteen years with my time, my means and all my heart. It was a community I loved, pouring into it my youth and my tears. That love even led me onto the path of theology, and wanting to serve more rightly, I became a student again at a theological graduate school far away in the United States. The deeper I dug into the Word, the clearer one thing became: the Bible alone must be at the center of everything.
그런데 제가 신학을 공부하던 바로 그 시간에, 사랑하던 그 교회가 <b: But during the very time I was studying theology, the church I loved was drifting, little by little, away from its essence. Gatherings to pray together were fading away, while members were eagerly urged to attend rallies for one of the world's political camps. The members' group chats filled up not with the gospel but entirely with political news. Politics had moved into the place where the gospel should be.
저는 더는 침묵할 수 없어, 조심스럽지만 분명하게 말씀드렸습니다. “교회: I could no longer stay silent, so I spoke — carefully, but clearly. “In every circumstance, the church must stay faithful to its essence: proclaiming the gospel. However hard things are for the nation, for the church to lean on a particular political force is, in God's sight, another form of idolatry.” It was a hard word spoken not out of dislike, but because I loved that church so deeply.
그 한마디의 대가는 가혹했습니다. 신학교 졸업을 코앞에 둔 어느 날, 저: The price of those words was harsh. One day, with my graduation from theological school just ahead, on a strange pretext, my name was struck from the membership roll of the community I had given fifteen years. The words “You never fit in with us from the start” pierced my heart like a dagger.
그러나 더 견디기 힘든 것은 그다음이었습니다. 십오 년을 형제요 자매라: But what was even harder to bear came next. The brothers and sisters in the faith whom I had called brother and sister for fifteen years, with whom I had wept and laughed, turned away from me overnight as if I were a stranger — no, as if I were an insect. What is the church, then, and what is faith? — I simply fell apart. Night after night I lay face down, weeping and pouring out my heart to God. And it wasn't only me. My beloved family were deeply wounded too, and for a time, under the shadow of panic, they could hardly even breathe.
그렇게 광야가 시작되었습니다. 어떤 권위도, 어떤 조직도, 십오 년의 정: And so the wilderness began. No authority, no organization, not even fifteen years of deep affection could protect me in the end. But in that very barren wilderness, God taught me the most precious thing of all: only those who read the Bible for themselves and stand on that Word will not be shaken in any storm.
그 깊은 어둠의 끝에서 드린 <b class=\"text-neutral-: At the end of that deep darkness, while I was fasting and praying, God poured into my heart a calling for these last days. With no grand pulpit and no large organization — that is how this ministry began: in tears. All I want is to help even one believer living in this last generation to stand rightly before the Word for themselves, without being swayed by anyone's interpretation.
저는 결코 뛰어난 사람이 아닙니다. 다만 광야에서 저를 붙드신, 부활이요: I am by no means an outstanding person. I am only a debtor to Him who held on to me in the wilderness — the One who is the resurrection and the life. I do not want my name to be lifted up in any of this. I pray that the Lord alone will be exalted, and that you who are reading this will stand rightly before God. If you know the same kind of pain, or if you long to love God sincerely — won't you walk this road together with me? Please stand with us in prayer. I ask you to walk alongside us on this journey of raising up unshakable believers and building healthy churches.
